newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BNDES appeals CVRD ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BNDES appeals CVRD ruling.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) on Tuesday appealed an injunction granted by the country's highest court that could lead to the suspension of the Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) privatization.

A spokeswoman for the Supreme Federal Tribunal said the bank lodged an appeal shortly after court minister Marco Aurelio de Mello ruled that the Carajas mining area could not be included in the CVRD auction.
The appeal would be heard by the judge, the spokeswoman said. Under the court's rules, an appeal against a judge's decision can only be heard by the judge himself.

If Mello rules in favor of BNDES, and against his own original verdict, the injunction would be quashed. But if he rules against the appeal, the government must wait until a full ruling on the issue by all 11 members of the Supreme Federal Tribunal.
The spokeswoman said she did not know how long Mello would take to rule on the appeal or when a full ruling might take place.
